day_shape: 71 items: US-Israel-Lebanon Trilateral Framework signed in Washington, CENTCOM strikes on Iran's southern coast in retaliation for Strait of Hormuz ship attack, Iranian MFA condemns ceasefire violation, IDF kills seven Hezbollah operatives in southern Lebanon, two UK Parliament questions tabled on Bahá'í persecution.

threads.label: Trilateral Framework signed in Washington
threads.summary: The US, Israel and Lebanon signed a Trilateral Framework at the State Department, with Secretary Rubio hosting the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors. Lebanese President Aoun called it a first step toward restoring Lebanese sovereignty, while Israeli ministers complained in cabinet about restrictions on IDF activity in Lebanon.

threads.label: US strikes on Iranian coast after Hormuz incident
threads.summary: CENTCOM announced military strikes against Iranian targets in retaliation for an Iranian attack on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz, which Trump called a 'foolish violation' of the ceasefire. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the strikes on its southern coastal surveillance facilities as a ceasefire violation, and parliament's national security chair Ibrahim Azizi said the president had no commitment to US negotiation principles.

threads.label: US-Iran MoU debate and regional realignment
threads.summary: Iran International and Jerusalem Post commentary examined the preliminary US-Iran memorandum of understanding ending the 70-day conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with analysts saying it freezes rather than resolves the nuclear dispute. Defa Press claimed CBS/YouGov polling showed US public opinion viewing Iran as the war's victor.

threads.label: IDF operations in southern Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF said its air force killed seven Hezbollah operatives near Manzala/El Manara who were moving weapons into a structure used as a combat and observation post. The military also reported striking six targets in southern Lebanon and killing at least ten in Gaza over the past week, and dropped warning flyers over Mansouri near Tyre.

threads.label: Khamenei succession messaging and funeral logistics
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted messages from Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei on national unity and standing against 'disbelief and arrogance,' while IRIB reported Tehran public transport made free for the 'Martyr Leader' farewell ceremony with police forecasting 30-35% population participation. Iran International reported Lebanon ordered removal of Beirut airport-road billboards depicting Mojtaba Khamenei and his late father.

threads.label: Iran internal: protests, banking, Baneh attack
threads.summary: Defa Press reported an armed attack on Baneh checkpoint killing a sergeant and a conscript and injuring a 3-year-old, while Iran International documented January protest victims traced to Gharazi Hospital in Isfahan and Muharram mourning recast for them. Shargh daily, cited by Iran International, said Iran's banks keep failing without explanation after repeat cyberattacks.

threads.label: UK Parliament questions on Bahá'í persecution
threads.summary: Liberal Democrat MP Tom Morrison tabled two written questions to the FCDO on Iran. One sought assessment of escalating persecution of the Bahá'í community; the other asked what steps were being taken with international partners to promote freedom of religion or belief for Bahá'ís.

events.summary_en: Role of China's "invisible hand" in preventing $200 oil At a time when Washington and Tehran are negotiating how to permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume the flow of Middle Eastern oil, the future of global oil prices is tied less to decisions made in American-Iranian negotiation rooms than to decisions by countries absent from these negotiations. One of the most delicate and at the same time most effective measures taken by the Chinese government in managing this crisis has been domestic policies in the refining and petroleum products sector. Beijing has severely restricted exports of refined products such as diesel and petrol to ensure energy security within its own borders and prevent fuel shortages.
